summary:
FireLens is an interactive web application and research prototype that makes differences between NASA MODIS and VIIRS active fire observations visible, inspectable, and reproducible. Because MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) differ in spatial resolution, sensitivity, and overpass timing, combining raw detections creates misleading fire trends.

Using real NASA FIRMS data for Kazakhstan (2024–2025), FireLens pairs an interactive multi-basemap viewer with a two-year activity calendar covering 76,422 QA-filtered detections across 24 monthly and 106 seven-day periods—keeping Aqua and NOAA-20 series separate rather than conflating raw counts. To test cross-sensor scaling transparently, we matched 4,032 nearby Aqua and NOAA-20 overpasses (≤60 min, ≤2 km), fitted a multiplicative FRP coefficient on 2024 data (0.431357), and evaluated it on held-out 2025 data, reducing RMSE from 84.71 to 70.49 MW/group while explicitly documenting bias and uncertainty.
details:
What FireLens Does & How It Works

A brighter fire map does not automatically mean more fires. FireLens brings real NASA FIRMS satellite observations, an interactive map, a two-year burning activity calendar, and a reproducible cross-sensor comparison experiment into a single bilingual (EN/RU) interface.

1. Interactive Map & Data Loading: Users can inspect satellite detections across four basemaps (Standard, Dark, Esri World Imagery, OpenTopoMap), search locations, select regional boundaries, import custom CSV/JSON files, or fetch recent FIRMS observations via a secure local server route.

2. Activity Calendar (Kazakhstan, 2024–2025): Aggregates 76,422 QA-filtered records (MODIS Aqua and VIIRS NOAA-20) into 24 monthly and 106 seven-day periods. Rather than summing raw detections across different sensors into misleading totals, FireLens keeps sensor series separate and lets users inspect exact calendar periods directly on the map.

3. Reproducible Cross-Sensor Experiment: To quantify how MODIS Aqua and VIIRS NOAA-20 Fire Radiative Power (FRP) compare, we matched nearby overpasses within 60 minutes and 2 km (4,032 matched groups). A scaling factor (0.431357) was fitted on 2024 data, frozen, and evaluated on held-out 2025 data (2,514 groups), improving FRP RMSE from 84.71 to 70.49 MW/group while transparently reporting mean bias (−20.92 MW/group) and bootstrap confidence intervals.

Intended Impact & Scientific Integrity

FireLens helps scientists, land managers, and emergency responders avoid misinterpreting sensor transitions as real changes in fire activity. Every dataset, calendar export (CSV/JSON), frozen model parameter, and SHA-256 input hash can be audited independently. We explicitly document scientific limitations: detection counts do not equal unique fires, missing records do not guarantee zero burning, and FireLens is a research prototype rather than an operational early-warning system.

Tools, Languages & Architecture

• Frontend & Visualization: HTML, СSS, JavaScript, Apache ECharts.

• Backend & Verification: Node.js, Express (server-side proxy protecting the NASA FIRMS MAP_KEY), Python & TypeScript audit scripts with automated CI verification (22 unit tests and SHA-256 hash checks).

• Data Sources: NASA FIRMS (MODIS Collection 6.1 Aqua & VIIRS 375m NOAA-20/S-NPP), Natural Earth boundaries, OpenFreeMap/OpenStreetMap, Esri World Imagery, OpenTopoMap, and Open-Meteo/GeoNames geocoding.
